case_title: Ohan Raj @ Dhand v. State of Haryana
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302 r/w s.34; s.392 r/w ss.395 and 397 (trial court convicted under s.302 r/w s.341 and s.392 r/w s.397)
evidence_type: Circumstantial evidence; extra-judicial confession of co-accused; disclosure statements and recovery; witness testimony (wife, brother, recovery witness); medical evidence
confession: Extra-judicial confession of co-accused (Sanjay) dated 4.2.1997 naming the appellants; earlier statement naming a different accomplice. Considered but NOT relied on; held misplaced and weak.
trial_court_outcome: Ohan Raj convicted: life imprisonment and Rs 2,000 fine under s.302 r/w s.341 IPC; 8 years RI and Rs 1,000 fine under s.392 r/w s.397 IPC; sentences concurrent. Co-accused Badal acquitted separately (18 Feb 2009).
high_court_outcome: Appeal of Ohan Raj dismissed (conviction upheld); State's appeal allowed and Badal convicted on same grounds
neutral_facts: The victim, a doctor posted at a village dispensary, left his home by car in January 1997 carrying a briefcase and a wrist watch. Later that day a dispenser at the dispensary informed the victim's brother that the victim's body had been found in a field in a nearby village. The body lay on its side with multiple injuries from a sharp-edged weapon, blood was on the ground nearby, and the victim's car was missing. The victim's brother lodged a first information report and a post-mortem was conducted. The post-mortem surgeon recorded seven injuries, opined that death resulted from shock and haemorrhage, and stated that a kirpan could have caused the injuries. A co-accused, held by another police force in a separate matter, made statements implicating two other men. His first statement named a different accomplice who had taken only the watch and briefcase, and the car was recovered on his disclosure. In a later statement he named the two men, saying one took the briefcase and the other the watch. Following disclosures, the two men were arrested and a briefcase and wrist watch were recovered. The victim's wife identified the items as belonging to her husband, stating that the watch bore initials. The victim's brother testified that three men arrived at the victim's house shortly after the victim left, asked for him, and gave their names. No footprints were found in the kutcha area where the body lay, and no other evidence placed the two men near the scene.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from multiple sharp-edged weapon injuries (seven injuries; shock and haemorrhage)
number_of_offences: 2 charged (s.302 and s.392, with related sections 34, 395, 397); 0 finally upheld
financial_property_loss: Victim's wrist watch, briefcase and Maruti car (car recovered from co-accused)
key_evidence_accepted: None accepted as establishing guilt. Court accepted only that the wrist watch and briefcase were missing from the victim and that the appellants may be in possession of stolen goods; medical opinion that a kirpan could cause the injuries was noted but not linked to the appellants.
witness_credibility: Recovery witness PW7 (wife) does not inspire confidence on identification of the watch. PW15 (victim's brother) is an interested witness whose statement is uncorroborated by any material.
post_offence_conduct: Co-accused Badal absconded and was declared a proclaimed offender before later arrest; disclosure statements led to recovery of items from the appellants
bail_history: Appellant in Crl. A. 703/2011 on bail granted by Supreme Court; appellant in Crl. A. 1410/2010 directed to be set at liberty if not required in any other case
trial_duration: offence: January 24, 1997; trial judgment: September 25, 1999 (Ohan Raj; Badal acquitted February 18, 2009); High Court: February 26, 2010; Supreme Court: May 9, 2014
legal_representation: Appellant: J. B. Mudgal and S. Rein (for R. C. Kaushik); State of Haryana (respondent): Samir Ali Khan
investigation_status: FIR No. 26 of 1997 registered; post-mortem conducted; investigation completed; challan presented; trial held
appeal_history: Trial court: Ohan Raj convicted, Badal acquitted. High Court: Ohan Raj's appeal dismissed; State's appeal allowed and Badal convicted. Supreme Court: appeals allowed, appellants acquitted.
defence_argument: At trial, the accused pleaded false implication and fabricated recovery (s.313 statement); no Supreme Court defence submissions recorded in the judgment
legal_principle_applied: Circumstantial evidence must form a complete unbroken chain consistent only with guilt; if more than one inference is possible, benefit of doubt goes to accused; extra-judicial confession of co-accused is weak evidence without cogent corroboration; recovery must relate to a fact connecting accused with the crime
precedent_relied_upon: Gopal Sah v. State of Bihar (2008) 17 SCC 128; Pancho v. State of Haryana (2011) 10 SCC 165; Sahadevan v. State of Tamil Nadu (2012) 6 SCC 403; Mano v. State of Tamil Nadu (2007) 13 SCC 795; Madhu v. State of Kerala (2012) 2 SCC 399; State of Rajasthan v. Talevar (2011) 11 SCC 666; Sharad Birdichand Sarda (1984) 4 SCC 116 (referred); Munish Mubar v. State of Haryana (2012) 10 SCC 464
other_sentence_order: Appellant in Crl. A. 1410/2010 to be set at liberty forthwith if not required in any other case
